evidence.snippet: export async function updateUserProfile(userId: string, data: UpdateUserProfileInput)
evidence.why: userId is accepted as a plain function parameter with no server-verified session to confirm the caller owns this id.

evidence.snippet: `UPDATE users SET ${setClauses.join(", ")}, updated_at = NOW() WHERE id = $1`, [userId, ...values]
evidence.why: The UPDATE uses the client-supplied userId as the sole identity/ownership predicate instead of a session-bound id, allowing any caller to update any user's profile.

evidence.snippet: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
evidence.why: No ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY or policy defined on the users table, leaving no database-level ownership enforcement as a backstop.

other_classes_observed: dynamic SQL column names built from object keys could allow unexpected columns if schema changes (low risk here since keys are from fixed zod schema)
